question: Halvard is commissioning a glass-washing skid aboard a research vessel. Its pump console shows E42 during the first rinse. The commissioning sheet records an inlet reading of 3.4 bar, taken before any restart attempt. A sealed replacement pump is available, but the voyage engineer will authorize only one next maintenance action. What should that action be, and what must the technician establish before approving a pump exchange?
required: restore inlet pressure to at least 4 bar
retest after restoring pressure
do not replace now
replace only if E42 persists after retesting with adequate inlet pressure
expected_answer: Restore the inlet pressure to at least 4 bar and retest before replacing anything. The current 3.4 bar reading is below the E42 threshold, so do not exchange the pump now. Replacement is justified only if inlet pressure is at least 4 bar and E42 persists after that retest.
rubric: Must prioritize restoring inadequate inlet pressure and retesting, reject immediate replacement, and give both the >=4 bar and persistent-after-retest prerequisites. No invented troubleshooting requirement may replace these steps.

question: A botanical conservatory uses a Halvard pump to feed a misting circuit. The afternoon handover records E42, an inlet gauge reading of 5.8 bar measured first, and a completed diagnostic rerun at that same reading; E42 appeared again. The facilities planner must choose between another inlet-supply adjustment and approving the pump exchange. Which disposition does the Halvard procedure require, and why?
required: replace the pump
5.8 bar meets the at least 4 bar inlet requirement
E42 persisted after retesting
expected_answer: Approve replacement of the pump. The inlet was checked first and 5.8 bar is at least 4 bar; E42 also persisted after a retest at that adequate inlet pressure. Both replacement prerequisites are satisfied.
rubric: Must approve pump replacement and justify it with adequate inlet pressure and the completed retest with persistent E42. Do not insist on an additional environmental repair or endless retests.

question: A travelling exhibition has a Halvard motion-control cabinet that reports R17 after its temporary power feed is connected. The electrician logs 20.7 V at the controller input. Nobody has rerun the cabinet diagnostics since that measurement. A courier can deliver a new controller before opening time. What should the exhibition crew do first, and what evidence would later justify accepting that replacement?
required: fix the supply to at least 22 V
retest after supply correction
do not replace the controller now
replace only if R17 persists after retesting with adequate supply
expected_answer: Correct the power supply to at least 22 V, then retest; do not replace the controller now. The recorded 20.7 V is below the R17 threshold. A controller replacement is justified only if supply voltage is at least 22 V and R17 persists after the retest.
rubric: Must address low supply voltage before changing the controller, require a retest after correction, and state the >=22 V plus persistent-R17 replacement condition. Courier availability is irrelevant.

question: At a remote materials-testing hut, a Halvard controller still displays R17. The signed service log says the supply was measured first at 22.8 V and remained there throughout a completed diagnostic rerun, which produced R17 again. The site has one spare controller and one spare power supply. Which spare should be used under the company rule? Explain which logged observations settle that choice.
required: replace the controller
22.8 V meets the at least 22 V requirement
R17 persisted after retesting
expected_answer: Use the spare controller. The supply was checked first and 22.8 V satisfies the at-least-22-V requirement, while R17 persisted after the diagnostic retest. The rule therefore calls for controller replacement, not a supply swap.
rubric: Must select controller replacement, identify adequate supply voltage and the persistent fault after a completed retest, and avoid choosing the supply as the required repair.

question: A film-restoration studio has moved its Halvard cooler into a temporary screening booth. T09 lights up after the booth is closed. Before any diagnostic rerun, a room sensor beside the unit records 35.8 C. The producer wants to replace the cooler before an evening screening. State the next action and the conditions that must be met before the studio can sign off on replacing the unit.
required: lower ambient temperature to at most 31 C
retest after lowering ambient temperature
do not replace the cooler now
replace only if T09 persists after retesting at acceptable ambient temperature
expected_answer: Lower the ambient temperature to at most 31 C and retest before replacing the cooler. The current 35.8 C exceeds the T09 environmental limit. Replacement is justified only if ambient temperature is at most 31 C and T09 persists after that retest.
rubric: Must lower the excessive ambient temperature first, require a new retest, reject immediate replacement, and state the <=31 C plus persistent-T09 replacement condition. Do not substitute an unsupported airflow-specific rule.

question: During installation of an audio mastering suite, a Halvard cooler reports T09. The commissioning record shows the ambient check came first: 28.6 C, unchanged through a completed diagnostic rerun. T09 was still present at the end. Procurement asks whether the crew must alter the room conditions again or can authorize the cooler exchange. Give the required disposition with its supporting conditions.
required: replace the cooler
28.6 C satisfies the at most 31 C ambient requirement
T09 persisted after retesting
expected_answer: Authorize replacement of the cooler. Ambient temperature was checked first and 28.6 C is at most 31 C, while T09 persisted after the completed retest. The environmental and retest prerequisites for replacement are met.
rubric: Must authorize cooler replacement and justify it with acceptable ambient temperature and persistent T09 after retesting. Do not demand another environmental correction when the stated prerequisites are already met.
